name: suite-query-failure-reconciliation
body:
Defect + reconciliation [verified against this branch's code graph and source; the brief's FQNs were the MAIN-checkout ones, corrected below].

Defect: opencode suite tools that shell out to `apg query` and parse its CSV output feed runCypher's error string straight into csvToRows. `runCypher` (opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts:54-68) returns `"Error: no apg/.trans/db.lbug found …"` or `"apg query failed (exit N):\n<message>"` on failure; `csvToRows` (apg.ts:132-139) is line-based, so the error parses as rows. `apg_plan_tasks` (opencode-suite/tools/apg_plan_tasks.ts:25-37) destructures the rows and calls `fqn.replace(...)` on an undefined `fqn` → `undefined is not an object (evaluating 'fqn.replace')`, masking the real `apg query failed` cause. Observed live by a reviewer whose apg_plan_tasks call hit a transient DB-lock error.

Dead-code guard: `isQueryError` (apg.ts:145-147) and `expectQueryOk` (apg.ts:155-158) already implement exactly this guard — expectQueryOk's doc comment names the identical prior crash `'body.replace'` — but NO tool imports them. Verified twice: a grep over opencode-suite finds only the definitions, and the code graph shows `expectQueryOk` has no callers (it is called by nothing; `isQueryError` is called only by `expectQueryOk`). The guard is dead code, so the class recurred.

Blast radius (source-verified, because the code graph does NOT resolve the cross-file tool→lib calls — the tools' anonymous `execute` arrows are not Function nodes, so `csvToRows` shows 0 callers and `runCypher` only its in-file callers): 3 tools parse CSV (`apg_plan_tasks`, `apg_plan`, `apg_plan_phases`); 14 more call runCypher and return/echo its output directly (a failure surfaces as raw error text, not a crash — inconsistent but not fatal).

What changed (spec-side only; no plan/task or feedback authored):
- Added `requirements.requirement.suite-tools-surface-query-failures` (feature `agent-refinement`), contained by `requirements.requirement.agent-refinement`, driving `domain.group.agent-suite`.
- Added `realised-by domain.group.agent-suite → solution.component.suite-tool-wrappers`, putting the suite-tool component on the agent-refinement spine so the requirement traces to it (Contains is not walked by the coverage gate, so the existing `cli-surface` Contains edge could not serve).
- Reconciled `solution.component.suite-tool-wrappers`'s body: the .ts files ARE scanned code here (File/Function nodes exist), so its "not scanned code in this graph" claim was stale — but the correction is NOT to anchor to them. Their FQNs are rooted at the checkout directory basename (`suite-query-error-guard.opencode-suite.lib.apg.runCypher` in this worktree vs `apg.opencode-suite.lib.apg.runCypher` on main), so a worktree-prefixed FQN is not a stable `implemented-by` anchor — it would be spec drift on the main rebuild, and `apg.layers.validate_code_refs` bails the scan on drift. The component therefore keeps its stable `implemented-by apg.main` embedding anchor.

Contradictions found vs the brief:
1. The brief's FQNs (`apg.opencode-suite.lib.apg.runCypher`) are the MAIN-checkout FQNs; on this branch the TS module prefix is the worktree dir basename (`suite-query-error-guard.`). This makes .ts FQNs unanchorable — the reason the suite-tool-wrappers body's literal claim is stale but its anchor is right.
2. The graph does not resolve the tool→lib Calls (see blast radius) — the crash sites are source facts, not graph facts; only `runCypher`/`csvToRows`/`isQueryError`/`expectQueryOk` resolve as scanned Functions in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts`.
3. The crash is confirmed in `apg_plan_tasks` (destructured `fqn` undefined). `apg_plan` and `apg_plan_phases` mis-parse the error into garbage and can hide the cause, but do not show the same `undefined.replace` crash on the destructured `fqn`.

Coverage note for the plan-writer: the change is to .ts content embedded by `apg.main` (`include_str!`), so the reached solution nodes (`solution.system.agent-suite` and `solution.component.suite-tool-wrappers`) resolve to the stable code FQN `apg.main`; the plan must carry a delivery-anchor task targeting `apg.main` for `apg plan verify` coverage to hold.
